title: New Winners at the New York City Marathon
summary:
Andreas Almgren from Sweden won the men's race at the New York City Marathon on Sunday. It was his first time running a full marathon, which is 26.2 miles long. He had run shorter half-marathons before. He pulled ahead of Yemaneberhan Crippa from Italy in the last mile and won in 2 hours, 6 minutes and 1 second. Crippa finished 13 seconds later. Kamohelo Mofolo from Lesotho came third, just ahead of last year's winner, Benson Kipruto. Almgren's time was the third fastest ever on this course.

Sheila Chepkirui from Kenya won the women's race for the second time. She ran past Hellen Obiri near the end and won in 2 hours, 24 minutes and 36 seconds. Jessica McClain from the United States finished second, six seconds behind. She was the first American woman in the top three since 2018.

About 60,000 runners from more than 140 countries took part. The race went through all five parts of New York City, called boroughs. It started in 1970 in Central Park. This year the course changed a little at Mile 20.
why_it_matters: Training for a long race shows how steady practice can help you reach a big goal.
